evidence.quote: Department of Psychiatry · UC San Diego School of Medicine Decoding the biology of addiction We identify the neurobiological mechanisms underlying drug addiction and develop novel pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatments to help people with substance use disorders. The Research Join the Lab 10 0 m 10 −9 m Nine orders of magnitude, one question 10 0 m Behavior & body Self-administration, vapor models, gut microbiome 10 −2 m Whole brain Light-sheet imaging, functional connectomics 10 −3 m Circuits Optogenetics, chemogenetics, deep brain stimulation 10 −6 m Synapses & cells Slice electrophysiology, neuronal ensembles 10 −9 m Genes & molecules GWAS, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, metabolomics Zoom through all nine scales → Single-cell whole-brain imaging of neuronal ensembles — one of the lab's signature approaches. The Approach From genes to behavior Multilevel & integrated GWAS, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, slice electrophysiology, whole-brain imaging, microbiome, and metabolomics — connected in the same animal models. The approaches Behavioral phenotyping at scale State-of-the-art animal models of addiction with the capacity to test more than 60 animals simultaneously, including pioneering vapor self-administration models. The models Toward new medications Pre-IND, proof-of-concept, and pharmacokinetic studies — plus deep brain stimulation and biologics — to turn mechanisms into treatments. The pipeline “From a single gene to the whole person, addiction touches every level of biology, so we study every level .” Explore the nine scales The evolution of the concept of addiction A century of addiction science How addiction went from a moral failing to be policed to a brain disorder to be diagnosed, studied, and treated, in 186 milestones from the 1900s to today. 1914 Policy & institutions Harrison Narcotics Tax Act 1935 Treatment & recovery Birth of Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) 1954 Neuroscience Brain reward circuits discovered 1997 Neuroscience Neurocircuitry Theories of Addiction - Allostasis and the "Dark Side" 2013 Epidemics & trends Opioid epidemic, wave 3: fentanyl Explore all 186 milestones Open Science Open to the field The Addiction Biobanks Specimens from more than 2,000 behaviorally and genetically characterized rats, vulnerable or resistant to cocaine and oxycodone addiction, open to collaborators. Request samples PARC Dr. George directs the Polysubstance Addiction Research Center, a NIDA P50 Center of Excellence at UC San Diego. Visit PARC Training From high school students to postdocs, nearly 200 scientists have trained in the lab since 2006. Positions open year-round.
